subject: art-design
title: Annotation & Analysis: Foundations
welcome_lead: Learn the questions to ask of any artwork — yours or someone else's.
meta_desc: GCSE foundations of annotation: media, formal elements, intention and influences.
final_note: Strong annotation turns looking into evidence of thinking.

concepts.def: Written notes that explain decisions and meaning.
Materials used to make a piece of work.
Line, shape, form, tone, colour, pattern, texture.
What the artist wanted the work to do or say.
Artist or idea that shaped the work.
Judging strengths, weaknesses and next steps.

walkthroughs.body_html: Start with the basics. Name the media (e.g. graphite on cartridge paper) and the subject. Then walk through the formal elements — what kinds of line, what tonal range, what colour palette, what textures.

State the intention: what mood or idea were you exploring? Reference any influences — a named artist, a movement, a place, a memory. Linking choices back to research shows examiners that your work is informed.

A good evaluation says what worked, what didn't and what you'll try next. Use phrases like "successful because…", "less effective where…" and "to develop this I will…". Avoid generic praise — be specific to the piece in front of you.
